questions.answer: A lot

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *

questions.answer: Very Americanised

questions.answer: Food is significantly cheaper, but other costs like housing, especially in Taipei, is also cheaper, but not by much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go with savings, as you'll get plenty of opportunities to travel a lot, and you'll easily spend loads there! (It's so so worth it)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The uni did have activities for students, clubs etc, and I did go in the start to make friends, but once you have your groups, idk, I just did other stuff with them, unrelated. But there's a lot of opportunities!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travelling! In Taiwan and around!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travelling? The islands are fun. They're underrated! Penghu, Green island, Orchid Island, Matsu, etc.!! Also, Yilan, I never got tired of going there, no matter how many times I went!! It's also only an hour from Taipei, so very ideal!! Wulai is Al'so worth a visit. But all this is easy to find in online guides...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Hmm first semester was definitely harder than the second! Making friends was hard in the beginning, but I used the app "Timeleft" and I got a whole friend group out of it, so that was nice!! The second semester was super easy and fun as the hard "adjustments" were over...

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Timeleft? The app... Oh and always bring an easy game like Uno or a set of cards with you everywhere, so there's something to do as you get to know locals, some of them can get a bit awkward in the beginning when they don't know what to do yet lol

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Loads... But I easily overcame them? A lot of bugs everywhere, indoors too... Ants, cockroaches, flying ones too... It's all a bit much in the beginning, but it gives you something to bond over with the other internationals

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, by far. Public transport in Taipei? Mountains? Accessibility to nature? I miss that a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The semester goes by very very quickly, almost by a blink of the eye... So enjoy it to the fullest. Always say yes to locals, they got some crazy fun ideas sometimes, and you'd rather not miss out on an insane hike in the mountains to some local hot springs!!! Locals are so open and fun, and very comfortable to hang out with, miss a lot of my friends from there!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Oh, there's a buddy programme you can sign up for too, not a bad idea, it can be a way in for local friends too... First uni, I met my "buddy" once, and then never again haha, but at my second stay, we are still in contact and did meet up quite a few times! So you never know

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The start, getting adjusted, making friends. Once you have found your place tho, it's amazing

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun, it's so fucking worth it

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
